title: Build, Release & Production
description: Review of the build system, versioning, release records, factory programming and provisioning, and the release package.

items.text: The build is reproducible from a tagged commit with a pinned toolchain
items.hint: A container or a documented toolchain version. Build twice and compare hashes.

items.text: Release builds come from CI, not a developer's machine
The version, git hash, and build date are embedded in the image and readable from the device
items.hint: Over the service port, the UI, or the cloud.

items.text: Version numbers follow a written scheme (e.g. semantic versioning)
items.hint: And the security version used for anti-rollback is separate from the display version.

items.text: Release and debug build settings are reviewed (optimization, asserts, logging, debug features)
The ELF, map file, and symbols are archived for every release
items.hint: Needed to decode crash dumps from the field.

items.text: The factory programming procedure, image, and fixture are documented and version-controlled
items.hint: Including the image hash the line should verify.

items.text: Production test firmware or test modes check every interface on the board
items.hint: Coordinate with the EE bring-up and the factory test plan.

items.text: Serial numbers, MAC addresses, and calibration are written and recorded per unit
items.hint: Traceable to the board, the image, and the test result.

items.text: Device locking (debug, read-out protection) is applied and verified at end of line
items.hint: An unlocked unit shipping is a security and IP leak.

items.text: Per-device keys and certificates are provisioned in a secure, logged step
items.hint: Keys never exist in plain files on factory PCs longer than needed.

items.text: Programming time per unit meets the line's cycle-time target
Release notes list changes, known issues, and the tested hardware revisions
The SBOM and license notices are produced for the release
items.hint: Open-source licenses may require notices in the product documentation or UI.

items.text: Source and build instructions are handed over as the contract requires
items.hint: Agree what the client receives: source, binaries, keys, toolchain.

items.text: Signing keys are held by the agreed owner, with a backup and access control
items.hint: Losing the signing key means no more updates. Agree with the client who holds it.
